reason: The C1 sentence pinned every control arm's score as the Linux receipts' score ('sequence 3/8'), but the sequence control is ORDER-DEPENDENT BY DESIGN: it answers with a fixed exit cycle [0,0,1,1,2,1,0,2] keyed by call index while the counter shuffles the class order, so its score is a property of the order drawn, not of the host. Attempt-1's own record already said 'sequence 3/8 (3-5/8 across runs, order-shuffled)'. The first scored family on this host drew an order scoring 1/8 (.ufo/evidence/round-60/win-host/first-family/ctl-sequence.out) — still red, still within the control's design, and the claim sentence as written was false on that clause. This amendment re-states the C1 sentence with the sequence arm described honestly; the counter bytes, cells, class set, expected exits and PASS condition are UNCHANGED (the kill rule's re-freeze trigger is counter change, which did not happen; the sentence correction is frozen here before the second scored family runs). Analysis recorded with mistake 7 in corpus/lessons/round-60.md: the cycle can align with the shuffled expecteds on 3!*3!*2!/8! = 1/560 of orders, where the control would score 8/8 and kill the counter per the kill rule — a per-run hazard attempt-1's freeze also carried, stated here so the kill rule is priced honestly.
